newsitem.title: USA: Simpson unable to explain blood, cuts on hand.
newsitem.headline: Simpson unable to explain blood, cuts on hand.

text.p: O.J. Simpson testified on Monday he had no explanation for blood found inside his Ford Bronco and at his estate, or for some of the cuts on his hand following the murders of his ex-wife and her friend.

During Simpson's second day on the witness stand in his civil trial, Daniel Petrocelli, lead attorney for the plaintiffs, mounted a scathing attack on the former football star's alibi for the night Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman were killed.

Simpson testified mostly in a calm, confident voice, but when asked about a phone call in which police informed him of his ex-wife's death, he squirmed uncomfortably, sighed heavily and spoke at times with a tremor in his voice.
Petrocelli confronted Simpson in dramatic fashion about blood found dripped in his Bronco, inside his mansion and on the driveway of his multimillion-dollar estate.

The attorney contended that some of the unexplained injuries to Simpson's fingers and hand were caused by fingernails "ripping into your skin," suggesting it happened in the death struggle between Simpson and his alleged victims.

Simpson, who on Friday emphatically denied killing his ex-wife and Goldman, was acquitted of the murders by a criminal court jury in October 1995. He is now facing a wrongful death civil suit brought by the victims' families, who are seeking substantial financial damages.

Simpson said he recalled seeing only one speck of blood on the little finger of his left hand just before he took a limousine to the airport for a flight to Chicago on the night of June 12, 1994. He said he could not remember how he sustained the injury but insisted he only saw one drop of blood from that wound on his kitchen counter.
"You don't have any explanation for blood matching your blood and DNA ... in that Bronco, do you?" Petrocelli asked in an accusatory tone.
"That's correct," Simpson said.
"You don't have any explanation of how the blood of Nicole was found on that carpet (in the Bronco)," Petrocelli insisted.
"No," Simpson replied.

Simpson's attorneys are expected to mount a defence based on a theory that the so-called "trail of blood" at the murder scene and at Simpson's estate was planted by police in a conspiracy to frame him.
Simpson testified he suffered a large gash to his middle finger of his left hand when he a broke a drinking glass in the bathroom of his Chicago hotel room after being told of his ex-wife's murder.

Petrocelli showed Simpson and the jury photos of several other cuts and abrasions on his left hand. Simpson denied the cuts were there when he returned from Chicago, but admitted he had no explanation for how he received them.
At one point he suggested his 7-year-old son, Justin, may have caused one of the marks when they were wrestling.

Petrocelli also attacked Simpson's alibi that he was home at the time of the murders, arguing the former running back had changed his story about vital evidence in the case, giving two different versions of where his cellular phone was on the night of the murders.

Petrocelli said Simpson had told police in an interview conducted the day after the murders that he had been driving in his Bronco and made a call on his cellular phone to his girlfriend, model Paula Barbieri.

But Simpson's cellular phone records showed the only call made that night was at 10:03 p.m., putting Simpson in the Bronco at that time, Petrocelli said. The plaintiffs' attorneys have attempted to prove the killings occurred around 10:35 or 10:40 p.m.
Simpson told police in the interview his last action before leaving for the airport was to take his cellular phone out of the Bronco. But on Monday he testified he had taken it out hours earlier.

But Simpson maintained the transcript of the police interview was incomplete, that what he told police was that at around 11 p.m. on June 12 he had taken his cellular phone accessories -- a carrying case, spare battery and an adaptor -- out of the Bronco.
